key_points: AMD states it has four reportable segments, plus an All Other category which is not a reportable segment.
The Data Center segment primarily includes server CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, FPGAs, and Adaptive SoC products.

title: AMD 2022 Form 10-K — MD&A Results of Operations: segment reporting change (p48)
key_points: During the second quarter of fiscal year 2022, AMD changed its reporting segments to align financial reporting with how it manages its business in strategic end markets.
The change is described as consistent with how the Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM), the CEO, assesses financial performance and allocates resources.
As a result of the change, AMD reports financial performance based on four reportable segments: Data Center, Client, Gaming, and Embedded.
Additional segment detail is cross-referenced to Note 4 – Segment Reporting in Part II, Item 8 of the Form 10-K.
The segment revenue table on this page shows FY2022 vs FY2021: Data Center $6,043M / $3,694M; Client $6,201M / $6,887M; Gaming $6,805M / $5,607M; Embedded $4,552M / $246M; Total $23,601M / $16,434M.

The segment operating income table on this page shows FY2022 vs FY2021: Data Center $1,848M / $991M; Client $1,190M / $2,088M; Gaming $953M / $934M; Embedded $2,252M / $44M; All Other $(4,979)M / $(409)M; Total $1,264M / $3,648M.
Data Center net revenue increased 64% in 2022, primarily driven by higher sales of EPYC server processors.

Client net revenue decreased 10% in 2022, primarily driven by a 24% decrease in unit shipments, partially offset by a 19% increase in average selling price; the shipment decline was attributed to challenging PC market conditions and significant inventory correction across the PC supply chain in the second half of 2022.
Client operating income fell to $1.2 billion from $2.1 billion, driven by lower revenue and higher operating expenses.
raw_excerpt: During the second quarter of fiscal year 2022, we changed our reporting segments to align our financial reporting with how we manage our business in strategic end markets. This is consistent with how our Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM) assesses our financial performance and allocates resources. As a result, we report our financial performance based on the following four reportable segments: Data Center, Client, Gaming, and Embedded.

title: AMD 2022 Form 10-K — Note 4 Segment Reporting: retrospective adjustment and segment scope (p67)
key_points: In the second quarter of fiscal year 2022, AMD updated its segment reporting structure to align financial reporting with the manner in which it manages its business in strategic end markets.
The disclosed measure of segment operating results was updated consistent with the revised manner in which the CODM assesses financial performance and allocates resources.
All prior-period segment data have been retrospectively adjusted — this is the direct basis for year-over-year comparability of the four new segments.
Data Center segment primarily includes server CPUs and GPUs, DPUs, FPGAs and Adaptive SoC products for data centers.
Client segment primarily includes CPUs, APUs (accelerated processing units integrating microprocessors and GPUs), and chipsets for desktop and notebook personal computers.
Gaming segment primarily includes discrete GPUs, semi-custom SoC products and development services.
Embedded segment primarily includes embedded CPUs and GPUs, FPGAs, and Adaptive SoC products.

In addition to the four reportable segments, AMD has an All Other category which is not a reportable segment; it primarily includes expenses and credits not allocated to reportable segments because the CODM does not consider them in evaluating segment performance.
All Other primarily includes amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, employee stock-based compensation expense, acquisition-related costs and licensing gain.
raw_excerpt: In the second quarter of fiscal year 2022, the Company updated its segment reporting structure to align financial reporting with the manner in which the Company manages its business in strategic end markets. ... All prior-period segment data have been retrospectively adjusted. The Company's four reportable segments are: • the Data Center segment, which primarily includes server CPUs and GPUs, DPUs, FPGAs and Adaptive SoC products for data centers; • the Client segment, which primarily includes CPUs, accelerated processing units that integrate microprocessors and GPUs (APUs), and chipsets for desktop and notebook personal computers; • the Gaming segment, which primarily includes discrete GPUs, semi-custom SoC products and development services; and • the Embedded segment, which primarily includes embedded CPUs and GPUs, FPGAs, and Adaptive SoC products.
